sources.title: Continuous low frequency anthropogenic sound (continuous noise indicator)

sources.title: Zero pollution and Biodiversity: First ever EU-wide limits for underwater noise
sources.used_for: R4-F23: agreed 29 November 2022; area-exposure threshold values for continuous and impulsive noise; status as recommendations feeding member-state marine strategies, not a per-device permitted level.
sources.quote: no more than 20% of a marine habitat can be exposed to impulsive noise over a given day

sources.title: The effect of low frequency noise on the behaviour of juvenile Sparus aurata
sources.publisher: Journal of the Acoustical Society of America 147(6):3795 (2020), DOI 10.1121/10.0001255
sources.used_for: R4-F8, R4-F33, R4-U3: the only species-specific noise-response data found for Sparus aurata; tank exposure at 63, 125, 500 and 1000 Hz, 140-150 dB re 1 uPa, with habituation at low frequencies after about 2 h.
sources.quote: white noise filtered in third-octave bands centred at 63, 125, 500, and 1000 Hz

sources.title: Hearing thresholds in European sea bass (Dicentrarchus labrax): new insights into auditory sensitivity
sources.publisher: Fish Physiology and Biochemistry 52(1):9 (2026), DOI 10.1007/s10695-025-01628-2, via PubMed Central
sources.used_for: R4-F7, R4-U2: proxy audiogram for a Mediterranean farmed species; AEP on 114 juveniles at 100-600 Hz; best sensitivity 116.8 +/- 3.3 dB re 1 uPa at 300 Hz; states hearing data are lacking for many species.
sources.quote: Our results revealed a U-shaped audiogram with highest sensitivity at 300 Hz

sources.title: Managing Aquaculture Noise: Impacts on Fish Hearing, Welfare, and Mitigation Strategies
sources.publisher: Duan et al., Ocean University of China; Zenodo record 13325653, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.13325653 (journal version Reviews in Aquaculture, DOI 10.1111/raq.70013)
sources.used_for: R4-F9: farm equipment noise sits below 2000 Hz and overlaps the hearing range of most cultured species, supporting a low-frequency-generalist treatment of Sparus aurata.
sources.quote: particularly below 2000 Hz, matching the hearing range of most cultured species

sources.title: Fish Predation in Bivalve Aquaculture: Impacts and Potential Mitigation Strategies
sources.publisher: Stobart, Jeffs and Skelton, Reviews in Aquaculture (2025), DOI 10.1111/raq.70028, Wiley
sources.used_for: R4-F30, R4-F33: publisher full text returned HTTP 403; abstract read. Crop losses up to 100 percent; four mitigation categories; the French acoustic device initially effective then habituated, reported as unpublished personal communication.
sources.quote: Fish predation poses a significant challenge to bivalve aquaculture throughout the global range of production

sources.title: Acoustic Device Helps Prevent Sea Bream Damage to Shellfish Farms
sources.publisher: The Fish Site (reporting on Ifremer PREDADOR)
sources.used_for: R4-F29, R4-O10: Ifremer prototype adapted from a cetacean pinger, tested 2013 and 2014 for five months in Rade de Brest and Bay of Quiberon; no frequency, level, duty cycle or loss-reduction figure published.
sources.quote: a range of between 200 and 300 metres

sources.title: Aquaculture - use and efficacy of Acoustic Deterrent Devices (ADDs): report, Introduction
sources.used_for: R4-F31, R4-U10, R4-O11: little evidence for long-term ADD use; habituation to common signal types; dinner-bell effect; device-dependent results including 70 percent and 50 percent depredation reductions and one device with no effect; non-target cetacean disturbance.
sources.quote: there is currently little scientific evidence to support their long-term use.
